newsitem.title: INDIA: India to release new capital flows guidelines.
newsitem.headline: India to release new capital flows guidelines.

text.p: India will release new guidelines on outward capital flows on Thursday, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said.
"The new guidelines are being released in Delhi today," Chidambaram told reporters at a news conference in Bombay.
The new guidelines were not linked to the recommendations of the Tarapore committee on capital account convertibility of the rupee, Chidambaram said.
"The Tarapore report is a different issue entirely. We have been reviewing the guidelines. We reviewed them last July, we have reviewed them this year," Chidambaram added.
Chidambaram had told the Economic Times daily on Wednesday that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s rising forex reserves had prompted him to liberalise outward investment flows.
The RBI reserves have touched $28.22 billion on June 6, including gold and special drawing rights.

"We must do something constructive with our increasing dollar reserves and one way of productively deploying them is to allow a more liberal outward investment flow," the newspaper quoted Chidambaram as saying.
He called for the excess dollars in the system to be used for increased imports of capital goods, intermediates and technology, the paper added.
